method: COMPILED FROM 2 SOURCES. S1: QUOTED from Paget's Association (UK)-led Guideline Development Group (Ralston SH et al.), Journal of Bone and Mineral Research 'Diagnosis and Management of Paget's Disease of Bone in Adults: A Clinical Guideline' (published 25 February 2019 (vol 34, issue 4)), 19 claims; LICENCE: CC BY 4.0 (read at Europe PMC fullTextXML <license> element for PMC6522384). S2: PARAPHRASED AND HASH-ANCHORED from Britton C, Walsh J, Australian Family Physician 41(3):100-103 (PMID 22396921) 'Paget disease of bone - an update' (March 2012), 9 claims; LICENCE: © The Royal Australian College of General Practitioners (free to read; no open licence) (read at the racgp.org.au article page footer). Verify each source separately: verify.py --source <file> --only-source S<n>. Source text: the article abstract (tags stripped) followed by the body text from pmc_text.py, both from the Europe PMC JATS XML. Edition 2.0 adds S2, an Australian clinical review (Australian Family Physician 2012, © RACGP, free to read), paraphrased and hash-anchored from the racgp.org.au HTML with tags stripped; its Table 3 (indications and doses) survived as text. It is not a guideline and predates S1. The Endocrine Society 2014 guideline (CC BY-NC-ND) was tried and returned a bot challenge at academic.oup.com. No Australian Paget guideline was found. The S1 claims are unchanged.

claims.claim: **Paget disease is a non-malignant disorder of focal, abnormal bone remodelling** at one site (monostotic) or several (polyostotic). It favours the pelvis, spine, femur, tibia and skull.
claims.source_text: Paget's disease of the bone is a nonmalignant skeletal disorder characterized by focal abnormalities in bone remodeling at one (monostotic) or more (polyostotic) skeletal sites. Almost any bone can be affected, but there is a predilection for the pelvis, spine, femur, tibia, and skull.
claims.locator: Paget's Association (UK)-led Guideline Development Group (Ralston SH et al.), Journal of Bone and Mineral Research, 'Diagnosis and Management of Paget's Disease of Bone in Adults: A Clinical Guideline', published 25 February 2019 (vol 34, issue 4), https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6522384/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Bone pain in Paget disease is complex:** it goes with high bone turnover but can occur without it. Analgesics, NSAIDs and anti-neuropathic drugs are widely used but have not been tested in controlled trials.
claims.source_text: Bone pain in PDB is a complex symptom that is associated with increased bone turnover but that may also occur in patients without increased metabolic activity. … Although other drugs such as analgesics, nonsteroidal anti‐inflammatory drugs, and anti‐neuropathic agents are often used in the management of bone pain associated with PDB, these agents haven't been investigated in controlled clinical trials.
claims.locator: Paget's Association (UK)-led Guideline Development Group (Ralston SH et al.), Journal of Bone and Mineral Research, 'Diagnosis and Management of Paget's Disease of Bone in Adults: A Clinical Guideline', published 25 February 2019 (vol 34, issue 4), https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6522384/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Screen with serum total alkaline phosphatase (ALP) plus liver function tests** to look for metabolically active disease.
claims.source_text: 2) Serum total alkaline phosphatase (ALP) is recommended as a first‐line biochemical screening test in combination with liver function tests in screening for the presence of metabolically active PDB.
claims.locator: Paget's Association (UK)-led Guideline Development Group (Ralston SH et al.), Journal of Bone and Mineral Research, 'Diagnosis and Management of Paget's Disease of Bone in Adults: A Clinical Guideline', published 25 February 2019 (vol 34, issue 4), https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6522384/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **A normal ALP does not exclude Paget disease.** In the only population study, total ALP had a sensitivity of 57.7%; only 11 of 26 people (42%) with radiological Paget disease had a raised ALP.
claims.source_text: It showed that the sensitivity of total ALP was 57.7% (95% CI 38.9-74.5); specificity 88.9% … It's also important to emphasize that of 26 patients with radiological features of PDB, only 11 (42%) had elevated total ALP concentrations.
claims.locator: Paget's Association (UK)-led Guideline Development Group (Ralston SH et al.), Journal of Bone and Mineral Research, 'Diagnosis and Management of Paget's Disease of Bone in Adults: A Clinical Guideline', published 25 February 2019 (vol 34, issue 4), https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6522384/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Bone turnover markers rise in many diseases**, so they cannot diagnose Paget disease on their own.
claims.source_text: It should be noted, however, that elevations in markers of bone turnover occur in many disease states and cannot be used in isolation for the diagnosis of PDB.
claims.locator: Paget's Association (UK)-led Guideline Development Group (Ralston SH et al.), Journal of Bone and Mineral Research, 'Diagnosis and Management of Paget's Disease of Bone in Adults: A Clinical Guideline', published 25 February 2019 (vol 34, issue 4), https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6522384/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Use a radionuclide bone scan as well as targeted X-rays** to fully and accurately map metabolically active disease.
claims.source_text: 1) Radionuclide bone scans, in addition to targeted radiographs, are recommended as a means of fully and accurately defining the extent of metabolically active disease in patients with PDB.
claims.locator: Paget's Association (UK)-led Guideline Development Group (Ralston SH et al.), Journal of Bone and Mineral Research, 'Diagnosis and Management of Paget's Disease of Bone in Adults: A Clinical Guideline', published 25 February 2019 (vol 34, issue 4), https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6522384/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **X-ray features are non-specific one by one but usually diagnostic in combination.**
claims.source_text: Individually, these features are not specific, but when they occur in combination, they are usually diagnostic.
claims.locator: Paget's Association (UK)-led Guideline Development Group (Ralston SH et al.), Journal of Bone and Mineral Research, 'Diagnosis and Management of Paget's Disease of Bone in Adults: A Clinical Guideline', published 25 February 2019 (vol 34, issue 4), https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6522384/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **MRI and CT are not usually needed for diagnosis** but are very useful for complications: basilar invagination, spinal stenosis and osteosarcoma.
claims.source_text: Although the use of MR imaging and CT imaging is not generally indicated for the diagnosis of PDB, clinical experience indicates that MRI and/or CT imaging is very useful for the investigation of several complications of PDB, including basilar invagination, spinal stenosis, and osteosarcoma.
claims.locator: Paget's Association (UK)-led Guideline Development Group (Ralston SH et al.), Journal of Bone and Mineral Research, 'Diagnosis and Management of Paget's Disease of Bone in Adults: A Clinical Guideline', published 25 February 2019 (vol 34, issue 4), https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6522384/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: 🇦🇺 **Common in Australia:** Paget disease affects 2–4% of adults over 55 and is common in countries with much British ancestry, including Australia; no recent Australian prevalence study exists. It is now usually found by chance (raised ALP or an X-ray); lifetime osteosarcoma risk is under 1%.
claims.locator: Britton C, Walsh J, Australian Family Physician 41(3):100-103 (PMID 22396921), 'Paget disease of bone - an update', March 2012, https://www.racgp.org.au/afp/2012/march/paget-disease-of-bone, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: ⚠️ 🇦🇺 **Check 25-hydroxyvitamin D:** osteomalacia can also cause bone pain with a raised ALP, and vitamin D deficiency must be corrected before a bisphosphonate to avoid hypocalcaemia. In liver disease, ALP isoenzymes or bone resorption markers help.
claims.locator: Britton C, Walsh J, Australian Family Physician 41(3):100-103 (PMID 22396921), 'Paget disease of bone - an update', March 2012, https://www.racgp.org.au/afp/2012/march/paget-disease-of-bone, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Bisphosphonates are recommended for Paget bone pain, and zoledronic acid is the one most likely to relieve it.**
claims.source_text: 3) Bisphosphonates are recommended for the treatment of bone pain associated with PDB. Zoledronic acid is recommended as the bisphosphonate most likely to give a favorable pain response.
claims.locator: Paget's Association (UK)-led Guideline Development Group (Ralston SH et al.), Journal of Bone and Mineral Research, 'Diagnosis and Management of Paget's Disease of Bone in Adults: A Clinical Guideline', published 25 February 2019 (vol 34, issue 4), https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6522384/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **In a double-blind trial of 357 patients, one 5 mg IV dose of zoledronic acid relieved pain more often than oral risedronate 30 mg daily for 2 months** (RR = 1.36).
claims.source_text: Another randomized double‐blind study involving 357 patients published by Reid and colleagues showed that zoledronic acid given as a single dose of 5 mg intravenously was more likely to give pain relief than risedronate sodium 30 mg daily orally for 2 months (RR = 1.36
claims.locator: Paget's Association (UK)-led Guideline Development Group (Ralston SH et al.), Journal of Bone and Mineral Research, 'Diagnosis and Management of Paget's Disease of Bone in Adults: A Clinical Guideline', published 25 February 2019 (vol 34, issue 4), https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6522384/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **The effect lasts:** 5 years after a single 5 mg zoledronic acid dose, 88% still had a normal total ALP, against 47% after oral risedronate (extension study, high attrition).
claims.source_text: 88% of patients treated with a single dose of 5 mg zoledronic acid intravenously still had a normal serum total ALP after 5 years' follow‐up compared with 47% of patients treated with oral risedronate sodium. … It should be noted that the attrition rate in this study was high
claims.locator: Paget's Association (UK)-led Guideline Development Group (Ralston SH et al.), Journal of Bone and Mineral Research, 'Diagnosis and Management of Paget's Disease of Bone in Adults: A Clinical Guideline', published 25 February 2019 (vol 34, issue 4), https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6522384/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Treat symptoms, not the ALP number.** A symptom-directed strategy is recommended over treat-to-target ALP normalisation; in PRISM, clinical fractures were similar in both arms.
claims.source_text: 4) Treatment aimed at improving symptoms is recommended over a treat‐to‐target strategy aimed at normalizing total ALP in PDB. … The number of clinical fractures in the intensive and symptomatic PRISM treatment arms were similar.
claims.locator: Paget's Association (UK)-led Guideline Development Group (Ralston SH et al.), Journal of Bone and Mineral Research, 'Diagnosis and Management of Paget's Disease of Bone in Adults: A Clinical Guideline', published 25 February 2019 (vol 34, issue 4), https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6522384/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **No trial or observational study shows that treating asymptomatic, metabolically active disease prevents complications.**
claims.source_text: we found no clinical trials or observational studies that specifically addressed the issue of whether treatment of asymptomatic patients with bisphosphonates that have metabolically active PDB was of benefit in preventing complications of the disease.
claims.locator: Paget's Association (UK)-led Guideline Development Group (Ralston SH et al.), Journal of Bone and Mineral Research, 'Diagnosis and Management of Paget's Disease of Bone in Adults: A Clinical Guideline', published 25 February 2019 (vol 34, issue 4), https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6522384/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Calcitonin has no randomised evidence against placebo or other osteoclast inhibitors,** and long-term calcitonin for osteoporosis has been linked to a higher risk of some cancers.
claims.source_text: No randomized trials were identified in which the effects of calcitonin were compared with placebo or with other osteoclast inhibitors. … Since these early reports, long‐term calcitonin therapy for osteoporosis has been associated with an increased risk of certain cancers.
claims.locator: Paget's Association (UK)-led Guideline Development Group (Ralston SH et al.), Journal of Bone and Mineral Research, 'Diagnosis and Management of Paget's Disease of Bone in Adults: A Clinical Guideline', published 25 February 2019 (vol 34, issue 4), https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6522384/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Denosumab 60 mg subcutaneously every 6 months rests only on two case reports,** in patients who could not take bisphosphonates; ALP and bone pain improved.
claims.source_text: There have been two case reports in the use of denosumab 60 mg by subcutaneous injection every 6 months in PDB in patients where bisphosphonates were poorly tolerated or contraindicated. In both cases, denosumab resulted in a decrease in total ALP concentrations and an improvement of bone pain.
claims.locator: Paget's Association (UK)-led Guideline Development Group (Ralston SH et al.), Journal of Bone and Mineral Research, 'Diagnosis and Management of Paget's Disease of Bone in Adults: A Clinical Guideline', published 25 February 2019 (vol 34, issue 4), https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6522384/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: 🇦🇺 **Who to treat (S2):** symptomatic disease (PBS-subsidised); a trial of therapy when pain localises to pagetic bone. S2 also argues for treating **asymptomatic** disease in the long bones, vertebrae or skull base, and younger patients with joint involvement such as the hip, to prevent complications. ⚠️ S1 found no evidence that this prevents complications.
claims.locator: Britton C, Walsh J, Australian Family Physician 41(3):100-103 (PMID 22396921), 'Paget disease of bone - an update', March 2012, https://www.racgp.org.au/afp/2012/march/paget-disease-of-bone, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: 🇦🇺 **Give a bisphosphonate before elective surgery** (such as joint replacement) on metabolically active pagetic bone, to reduce bleeding. (S2)
claims.locator: Britton C, Walsh J, Australian Family Physician 41(3):100-103 (PMID 22396921), 'Paget disease of bone - an update', March 2012, https://www.racgp.org.au/afp/2012/march/paget-disease-of-bone, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: 🇦🇺 **Australian regimens (S2):** zoledronic acid 5 mg IV once, infused over at least 15 minutes; or oral alendronate 40 mg daily for 3–6 months; or oral risedronate 30 mg daily for 2 months. Oral courses are stopped at remission, not continued long term. Pamidronate has largely been replaced by zoledronic acid; etidronate, tiludronate and calcitonin are largely obsolete.
claims.locator: Britton C, Walsh J, Australian Family Physician 41(3):100-103 (PMID 22396921), 'Paget disease of bone - an update', March 2012, https://www.racgp.org.au/afp/2012/march/paget-disease-of-bone, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: 🇦🇺 **Zoledronic acid is probably the treatment of choice (S2):** in the key trial ALP normalised in 89% vs 58% with 2 months of risedronate, and at 6.5 years 0.7% vs 20% had relapsed. Oral drugs remain reasonable if preferred or if IV treatment is unavailable.
claims.locator: Britton C, Walsh J, Australian Family Physician 41(3):100-103 (PMID 22396921), 'Paget disease of bone - an update', March 2012, https://www.racgp.org.au/afp/2012/march/paget-disease-of-bone, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Zoledronic acid's commonest adverse effect is a transient flu-like illness,** which is milder after the second and later infusions than after the first.
claims.source_text: The most common adverse event in studies with zoledronic acid was a transient flu‐like illness. … There is good evidence that the flu‐like symptoms are milder after second and subsequent infusions of zoledronic acid compared with the first infusion.
claims.locator: Paget's Association (UK)-led Guideline Development Group (Ralston SH et al.), Journal of Bone and Mineral Research, 'Diagnosis and Management of Paget's Disease of Bone in Adults: A Clinical Guideline', published 25 February 2019 (vol 34, issue 4), https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6522384/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Osteonecrosis of the jaw is very rare in Paget disease:** estimated at 0.0004% to 0.06% with oral bisphosphonates, far lower than in osteoporosis.
claims.source_text: The estimated frequency of osteonecrosis of the jaw (ONJ) in people with PDB receiving oral bisphosphonates was estimated as between 0.0004% and 0.06%, which is much lower than in osteoporosis.
claims.locator: Paget's Association (UK)-led Guideline Development Group (Ralston SH et al.), Journal of Bone and Mineral Research, 'Diagnosis and Management of Paget's Disease of Bone in Adults: A Clinical Guideline', published 25 February 2019 (vol 34, issue 4), https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6522384/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: 🇦🇺 **IV bisphosphonate side effects (S2):** a transient flu-like illness in about one in 4; rarely acute kidney failure or uveitis (past uveitis is a contraindication). Take oral bisphosphonates fasting, half an hour ahead of food and separate from other drugs; they can cause dyspepsia and, occasionally, oesophageal ulcers. Estimated jaw osteonecrosis risk ranges from one in 100 000 to one in 10 000.
claims.locator: Britton C, Walsh J, Australian Family Physician 41(3):100-103 (PMID 22396921), 'Paget disease of bone - an update', March 2012, https://www.racgp.org.au/afp/2012/march/paget-disease-of-bone, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: 🇦🇺 **Monitor ALP every 3–6 months until normal, then yearly once treatment stops (S2).** Relapse is common, can come years later and merits re-treatment; recurrent pain or progressing lytic lesions may precede a rise in ALP. (S1 favours treating symptoms over an ALP target.)
claims.locator: Britton C, Walsh J, Australian Family Physician 41(3):100-103 (PMID 22396921), 'Paget disease of bone - an update', March 2012, https://www.racgp.org.au/afp/2012/march/paget-disease-of-bone, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: 🇦🇺 **Do not neglect non-drug measures:** shoe raises or orthotics for leg shortening from deformity can help pain and gait. (S2)
claims.locator: Britton C, Walsh J, Australian Family Physician 41(3):100-103 (PMID 22396921), 'Paget disease of bone - an update', March 2012, https://www.racgp.org.au/afp/2012/march/paget-disease-of-bone, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Offer total hip or knee replacement for osteoarthritis when medical treatment is not enough.** No surgical approach is favoured over another.
claims.source_text: 5) Total hip or knee replacements are recommended for patients with PDB who develop osteoarthritis in whom medical treatment is inadequate. There is insufficient information to recommend one type of surgical approach over another.
claims.locator: Paget's Association (UK)-led Guideline Development Group (Ralston SH et al.), Journal of Bone and Mineral Research, 'Diagnosis and Management of Paget's Disease of Bone in Adults: A Clinical Guideline', published 25 February 2019 (vol 34, issue 4), https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6522384/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Femoral neck fractures through Pagetic bone often fail to unite:** non-union in 8 of 11 in one UK series and 11 of 11 in another.
claims.source_text: Most healed satisfactorily, but non‐union occurred in 8 of 11 (72.2%) patients with femoral neck fractures. … Most fractures healed satisfactorily, but non‐union occurred in 11 of 11 (100%) femoral neck fractures.
claims.locator: Paget's Association (UK)-led Guideline Development Group (Ralston SH et al.), Journal of Bone and Mineral Research, 'Diagnosis and Management of Paget's Disease of Bone in Adults: A Clinical Guideline', published 25 February 2019 (vol 34, issue 4), https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6522384/, retrieved 2026-09-23
